title: Honeybees dance directions, with straight up standing for the Sun
body: A forager that finds good flowers comes home and performs a **waggle dance** on the vertical comb, in the dark of the hive. The angle of her waggling run, measured from straight up, matches the angle between the food and the Sun outside. The longer the waggle lasts, the farther away the food is: in Karl von Frisch’s account, each second stands for roughly a kilometre. Bees that have been inside for a long time even shift the angle of their dance as the Sun moves across the sky.

cover.alt: Close-up of honeybee workers walking over golden honeycomb cells filled with honey

slides.alt: Animation on amber honeycomb: a map card shows flowers 40 degrees right of the Sun, then a stylised bee dances on the comb, her waggle run tilted 40 degrees from straight up. A stopwatch times the waggle for near and far food, and the angle turns as the Sun moves.

steps.label: A forager finds a rich patch of flowers
Back home, she dances on the vertical comb
Angle from 'up' shows angle from the Sun
A longer waggle means food farther away

slides.question: For Italian honeybees, beyond how many metres from the hive does a forager switch to the full waggle dance?
slides.explanation: Up to about 10 m she does a simple round dance, at 20 to 30 m a transitional dance, and beyond about 40 m the waggle dance.

slides.label: of dance followers in one experiment ignored the directions
slides.text: They flew back to places they already knew. Researchers still debate how much foragers rely on the dance itself rather than on smells or their own memories.

slides.heading: Doubted at first
slides.text: Karl von Frisch explained the dance in a 1927 book, but many scientists doubted him, and his work was appreciated only decades later. In 1973 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Konrad Lorenz and Nikolaas Tinbergen.

slides.question: A dancer's waggle run points 45° to the right of straight up. Where is the food?
options: 45° to the right of the Sun
45° to the left of the Sun
slides.explanation: On the comb, 'up' stands for the Sun's direction, so the angle of the run from vertical is the angle of the food from the Sun.
